name: Circle Loop
tagline: After the first circuit, every block becomes an exit.
description: A block-level computation-allocation method. All tokens complete the first circuit. A shared halter then uses the current state and its change to decide whether to continue, executing later core steps only for surviving tokens.
mechanism: 3 prelude + 9 core blocks + 3 coda, with 9–27 in-loop block executions
A target average core depth of 17.5; state-change features and unfolded-position biases inform halting
Exited states freeze and stop providing in-loop KV; the coda reunites all tokens
limitations: Differs from the earlier Circle-ST design that retained KV from exited tokens. Incremental KV-cache decoding is not implemented.
